label: B2B CRM — "We already have one"
objection: We've used Salesforce for years and the team finally knows it. Switching CRMs sounds like a huge disruption for not much gain.

exchanges.rep: Totally understand — a rip-and-replace is painful. Atlas isn't about replacing what works; most teams run it alongside their existing CRM and sync both ways during a phased rollout.
exchanges.reply: Okay, that's less scary than I assumed. But if it runs alongside Salesforce, what do my reps actually gain that they don't already have?

exchanges.rep: The big one is automatic activity capture — calls, emails, and meetings get logged without reps typing anything, so your pipeline data is finally complete and current.
exchanges.reply: Cleaner data would help, I'll admit. My worry is adoption — we rolled out a tool last year and half the team just ignored it. How is this different?

exchanges.rep: Fair concern. Because Atlas works inside the inbox and calendar your reps already live in, there's no new screen to remember — adoption tends to be passive rather than forced.
exchanges.reply: That makes sense. I'd want to see real adoption numbers from a team our size before I take this any further, though.

exchanges.rep: Absolutely — I can share two case studies from teams in your headcount range, plus set up a two-week pilot with your own data so you can judge adoption directly.
exchanges.reply: That's a fair offer. Let me loop in my team and review those case studies, and I'll get back to you on whether we run the pilot.

feedback.performance: You handled a tough incumbent objection well by reframing Atlas as complementary rather than a replacement, which lowered the customer's perceived risk. To strengthen further, quantify the gain earlier so the value is concrete before objections stack up.
feedback.key_strengths: You defused the switching-cost fear immediately and listened for the real blocker — adoption — then addressed it specifically rather than generically. Offering a pilot with the customer's own data was a strong, low-risk close.
feedback.areas_to_improve: Lead with a concrete, measurable outcome (e.g. hours saved per rep per week or pipeline accuracy lift) earlier in the conversation. Tying the 'we already have one' objection to a number the buyer cares about makes the case for a second tool far more compelling.
